title: Pseudococones on strict diagrams of small categories
statement: Let $J$ be a small category, $D:J\to\mathsf{Cat}$ a strict functor with small values, and $\mathcal A$ a category in a containing universe [def-nagata-category, def-weil-size-convention]. Define $\operatorname{PCone}(D,\mathcal A)$ to have objects the families of functors $A_j:D(j)\to\mathcal A$ with natural isomorphisms $\theta_a:A_kD(a)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_j$ for every $a:j\to k$, satisfying $\theta_{1_j}=1$ and $\theta_{ba}=\theta_a\circ(\theta_bD(a))$, using the strict identity and composition equalities of $D$. A morphism $(A,\theta)\to(B,\eta)$ is a family of natural transformations $\rho_j:A_j\to B_j$ satisfying $\rho_j\theta_a=\eta_a(\rho_kD(a))$. Such morphisms are equal exactly when their families are equal. Identities and composition are componentwise; their compatibility squares and the category laws hold. For a strict cocone $c=(C,v_j)$ of $D$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], define restriction $R_c:(C\to\mathcal A)\to\operatorname{PCone}(D,\mathcal A)$ by $R_c(F)_j=Fv_j$ and identity comparisons (the isomorphisms induced by $v_kD(a)=v_j$), and by whiskering on transformations. For every functor $H:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, postcomposition sends $(A,\theta)$ to $(HA,H\theta)$ and modifications to their images under $H$. A natural transformation $t:H\to H'$ induces the natural transformation between these postcomposition functors with component $t_{A_jx}$ at $(A,j,x)$. For every functor $w:K\to J$ between small categories, reindexing sends $(A,\theta)$ to $(A_{w(k)},\theta_{w(a)})$ and modifications to the reindexed families. These formulas satisfy the identity/composition coherence equations and modification compatibility squares required to define the stated functors and natural transformations.

proof.text: Modification equality follows by function extensionality on its transformation family and proof irrelevance of its compatibility field. Identity compatibility is the identity law. Composition compatibility follows by associativity and the two input modification squares; the category laws then hold componentwise.

For restriction, each comparison component is the image of an equality morphism. Functoriality of equality-to-morphism and proof irrelevance identify the normalization equation and the three equality morphisms in the composition equation. Naturality at the equality morphism gives compatibility of restricted transformations.

Apply the postcomposing functor to each coherence equation and each modification square, using preservation of composition. A transformation between postcomposing functors gives compatible components by its naturality at each comparison component, and is natural in pseudococones by naturality at each modification component.

For reindexing, substitute preservation of identities and composition by the index functor in the original coherence equations. Proof irrelevance identifies the equality transports supplied by the composite diagram. Modification squares and functor laws are the original componentwise ones at the reindexed objects and arrows.
